current_affair_article_art-1786448621261.translatedText: India is strengthening its Cultural Diplomacy

Cultural diplomacy uses culture to deepen mutual understanding and promote national interests through soft power, diaspora engagement, and strengthening relations.
Initiatives include the Global Engagement Scheme (GES), International Cultural Exchange Programme (ICEP), Project Mausam, and the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR).
Other efforts involve safeguarding intangible cultural heritage, restoring monuments abroad, Pravasi Bharatiya Divas, and the Know India Programme.

Cultural Diplomacy refers to use of culture as a strategic instrument to deepen mutual understanding, people-to-people ties and international partnerships.  

  • It includes exchange of ideas, values, traditions and other cultural or identity aspects to promote national interests. 

Significance/Need of Cultural Diplomacy

  • Soft Power: Enhances India’s global influence through Bollywood, yoga, cricket, cuisine and Indian arts. 
    • E.g., UN's declaration of International Day of Yoga.
  • Diaspora Engagement: Strengthens ties with the Indian diaspora and uses them as cultural bridges. E.g., India Day declared in Massachusetts, USA (2026). 
  • Strengthening Relations: Creates sustained cultural engagement that complements bilateral and multilateral diplomacy. E.g., India–ASEAN cultural exchanges (2026). 
  • Tourism & Economic Linkages: Promotes India’s heritage, cuisine, arts and traditions, supporting tourism and wider economic engagement. E.g., Buddhist Diplomacy with countries like Japan, Sri Lanka, etc. 

 

Initiatives taken to promote Cultural Diplomacy

  • Global Engagement Scheme (GES): Umbrella framework for bilateral and multilateral cultural cooperation. It includes- 
    • International Cultural Exchange Programme (ICEP): Festivals of India, artist exchanges and Cultural Exchange Programmes.
    • Project Mausam: Indian Ocean maritime cultural linkages.
    • Brihattar Bharat: Historical and civilisational cultural links.
    • Scheme for Safeguarding Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH): Preservation of intangible cultural heritage.
  • Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR): Promotes Indian culture abroad through cultural centres, exchanges and exhibitions.
  • Monument Restoration: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and Ministry of External Affairs collaborate to restore heritage sites abroad. E.g., Angkor Wat and Ta Prohm, Cambodia
  • Other: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD), Know India Programme (KIP) (Connects diaspora youth with India’s culture and heritage.
